newsitem.title: FRANCE: Delors says France would vote "no" to Maastricht.
newsitem.headline: Delors says France would vote "no" to Maastricht.

text.p: Former European Commission head Jacques Delors said on Sunday voters would reject European monetary union if a new referendum were held in France because the government was wrongly blaming it for current economic ills.
"There is an abusive identification between the difficulties of the French economy on one hand and Maastricht constraints on the other," the French Socialist told a conference on Europe.
Asked whether he believed French people would vote today for the Maastricht Treaty on European union, mapping out a path to a single currency from 1999, he said: "Today it would be lost in France".

France voted 51-49 percent in favour of the Maastricht Treaty in a 1992 referendum. Asked whether he reckoned French leaders were responsible for a slide away from the goals of the treaty, he said: "Of course".
Conservative Prime Minister Alain Juppe has imposed unpopular austerity policies to cut the French budget deficit in order to qualify for strict Maastricht economic criteria.

Delors, who did not run in the 1995 French presidential race won by Jacques Chirac despite polls showing he would have had a good chance of winning, said governments had to shift away from blaming Maastricht for austerity in Europe.
He said they should instead explain that budget rigour was needed to prevent young people from having to pay off today's debts in future.
